summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes, was admitted for acute-onset leg weakness and unsteadiness. Initial imaging ruled out spinal cord compression, but a brain MRI revealed multiple acute to subacute bilateral cerebral and cerebellar infarcts, consistent with embolic strokes likely originating from the heart due to atrial fibrillation. A transthoracic echocardiogram showed severe mitral annular calcification with possible thrombus, and carotid imaging confirmed complete occlusion of the right internal carotid artery, though not deemed the stroke source. Anticoagulation was switched from warfarin to apixaban due to subtherapeutic INR and high stroke risk. His kidney function remained stable, tacrolimus was adjusted for low trough levels, and torsemide was reduced to protect renal function. Physical therapy noted improvement in strength and balance, recommending inpatient rehabilitation. He was discharged to extended care with a plan for close follow-up and secondary stroke prevention.
problems: Cerebral infarction due to embolism of bilateral cerebellar arteries
Occlusion and stenosis of right carotid artery
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Enterocolitis due to Clostridium difficile, recurrent
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
